parole.significato: A foreigner; outlander.
parole.testo: Attested since 1890. From Afrikaans uitlander (“foreigner”), from Dutch uitlander (“foreigner”). Cognate and confluenced with outlander.

parole.significato: Vachellia haematoxylon, a southern African tree.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans valkameeldoring

parole.significato: A tourist from inland.
parole.testo: From Transvaal, from Afrikaans Vaal (“Vaal river”).

parole.significato: Very raw young wine, usually with sediment.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans [Term?], from Dutch vaal (“pale, cloudy”) + japie (“Jack or Jim”).

parole.significato: A shoe of untanned leather.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans.

parole.significato: Politically conservative.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans verkramp (“narrow, cramped”).

parole.significato: politically optimistic and receptive to change
parole.testo: From Afrikaans verlig from Dutch verlicht.

parole.significato: A person with a verlig (enlightened) political attitude.
parole.testo: Afrikaans

parole.significato: A deep-fried ball of dough, usually unsweetened, cut open and filled with various fillings.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans vetkoek (literally “fat-cake”).

parole.significato: The flowering plant Carpanthea pomeridiana.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans [Term?], from vet (“fat”) + kous (“sock”) + -ie, said to be an adaptation of a Khoekhoe name.

parole.significato: A plain.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans vlakte.

parole.significato: A shallow wetland or minor lake, generally a seasonal one, or the lowland where such a wetland appears seasonally.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans vlei, from Dutch vallei (“valley”). Doublet of valley and vly.

parole.significato: The crawling form of a locust, not yet able to fly.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans voetganger, from Dutch voetganger, from Middle Dutch voetganger.

parole.significato: get lost! go away! An exclamation of dismissal or rejection.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans voertsek, voortsek, short form(s) of voort sê ek (“go on I say”).

parole.significato: The Afrikaner people.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans volk. Doublet of folk.

parole.significato: A proposed state for Afrikaners, to be founded on principles of self-determination.
parole.testo: Afrikaans, literally "people-state".

parole.significato: A penis.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans voël (“bird”). Doublet of fowl.

parole.significato: rotten
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans vrot (“rotten”).

parole.significato: A woman.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans vrou. Doublet of frau, frow, and vrouw.

parole.significato: A native or inhabitant of the Free State in South Africa.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans [Term?].

parole.significato: Any plant of the subfamily Mesembryanthemoideae, succulent groundcovers.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans diminutive of vy(g) (“fig”), from Dutch vijg (“fig”).

parole.significato: A South African proteaceous tree (Protea nitida).
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans wagenboom, literally "wagon tree".

parole.significato: Any of certain plants with sharp hooked thorns found in southern and eastern Africa.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans wag-'n-bietjie.

parole.significato: The flower of Aponogeton distachyos.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans waterblommetjie (“small water flower”).

parole.significato: A South African stew of meat, typically lamb, with waterblommetjies.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans waterblommetjiebredie, literally meaning "small water flower stew".

parole.significato: Syzygium cordatum, a tree typically growing out of wet ground.
parole.testo: Afrikaans or English water + Afrikaans boom (“tree”)

parole.significato: A species of antelope endemic to Africa, Kobus ellipsiprymnus.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans waterbok, after the animal's habit of escaping to waterways.

parole.significato: The gnu.
parole.testo: Borrowed in the early 19th century from early Afrikaans wildebeest, modern wildebees (literally “wild ox”), with influence from beast.

parole.significato: Burchellia bubalina, the wild pomegranate.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans wildegranaat, from wilde granaat (“wild pomegranate”).

parole.significato: Home-distilled brandy or raw spirit, colourless and with a powerful kick.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans wit (“white”) + blits (“lightning”).

parole.significato: Members of conservative black vigilante groups in the South African provinces of the Cape and Orange Free State in the…
parole.testo: From Afrikaans wit (“white”) + doek (“cloth”), referring to the strips of white cloth members wore on their heads or arms.

parole.significato: Synonym of motlopi.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans witgat.

parole.significato: A scalp disease similar to favus, characterised by hair loss and white crust.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans witkop.

parole.significato: boerewors
parole.testo: From Afrikaans wors, from Dutch worst (“sausage”). Doublet of wurst.

parole.significato: A white South African man.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans japie, short for plaasjapie (“farm-boy”), referring to any person who grew up on a farm and is unfamiliar with city life, and hence naive and unsophisticated.

parole.significato: An exclamation used to express shock or exasperation.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans jere, a minced oath or alteration of Heere or Here (“Lord, God”, interjection), derived from Heer (“Lord”).

parole.significato: Expresses surprise, wonder, admiration, frustration, shock, or distress.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans and Xhosa.

parole.significato: Dodonaea thunbergii; Dodonaea angustifolia.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans ysterbos.

parole.significato: Money.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans sak (“bag”). Doublet of sac and sack.

parole.significato: A member of the South African Republic Police
parole.testo: From Afrikaans Zuid-Afrikaansche Republiek Politie.

parole.significato: Synonym of sitting room.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans sitkamer, from Dutch zitkamer.

parole.significato: A cannabis cigarette.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans zol.

parole.significato: A small bowl or container, sometimes with a cover such as a Tupperware container.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans bakkie, and then either: * from Northern Dutch bakkie (informal), from Dutch bakje (“container; drinking vessel; (archaic) carriage for passengers”), from bak (“container; drinking vessel; vehicle; part of a vehicle for carrying loads; part of a carriage for carrying passenge

parole.significato: To creep up on; stalk
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans bekruip, or alternatively from Dutch bekruipen, both from Middle Dutch becrûpen, equivalent to be- + creep.

parole.significato: A thick stew of meat and vegetables.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans bredie, possibly from Portuguese bredo. Alternatively, perhaps from Malagasy.

parole.significato: Synonym of Mpondo (“a Bantu people group indigenous to South Africa or a member of it”).
parole.testo: Uncertain. Probably from Xhosa amaMbo or Zulu amaMbo affixed with the Afrikaans -ie diminutive; compare Tambookie. Alternatively a Khoekhoe term. First attested in 1786.

parole.significato: A hot relish made from chili peppers and other ingredients.
parole.testo: Borrowed, either directly or via Afrikaans sambal, from Malay sambal, from Javanese ꦱꦩ꧀ꦧꦼꦭ꧀ (sambel).

parole.significato: The open grassland or pastureland of South Africa and neighbouring countries.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans veld, or from its etymon Dutch veld (“field; open country”) (formerly spelled veldt), ultimately from Proto-Germanic *felþuz (“field, plain”), possibly from Proto-Indo-European *pleh₂- (“flat”). Doublet of field.
